q: 1. Inflation is normally phenomenon in which ......
options: nominal price of object is raised
nominal price of objects is decreased
nominal price of object is constant
explain: Inflation is a sustained rise in the general (nominal) price level, so each unit of money buys less.

q: 2. Financial closure of a project means ......
options: signing the letter of interest to finance
signing for approval of a loan and commitment to fund the project
explain: Financial closure is reached when the loan/financing agreements are signed and the lenders commit to fund the project.

q: 3. Two projects having the same status expect payback period which project will be selected?
options: The project having more payback period
The project having less payback period
All off all of the above
explain: If everything else is equal, the project that recovers its investment sooner (shorter payback period) is preferred because it carries less risk and returns cash faster.

q: 4. The number of year from commissioning of the project at which net operating benefit equals to the investment is called ......
explain: Payback period is the time, counted from commissioning, after which cumulative net operating benefit equals the investment.

q: 5. The number of years required for the net operating benefit to pay back the initial cost of project is called ......
explain: This is the definition of payback period: years needed for net operating benefits to recover the initial cost.

q: 6. Pay Back period is counted only after ......
options: starting of the construction of a project
completion of the construction of project
explain: Benefits begin only when the project is commissioned, so the payback period is counted from commissioning, not from tendering or construction.

q: 7. For the selection of a project B/C ratio should be ......
explain: A project is acceptable when present worth of benefits exceeds present worth of costs, i.e. B/C > 1.

q: 8. In a project selection, minimum B/C ratio should be ......
explain: The minimum (threshold) B/C ratio is 1, where benefits just equal costs. Note: strictly, B/C above 1 is preferred; the key gives the threshold value.

q: 9. The minimum value of benefit cost ratio for selection of any project should ...... for acceptation of project.
explain: The minimum acceptable B/C ratio is equal to 1 (break-even). Below 1 the project is rejected. Note: this is the same idea as Q8; the key marks b.

q: 10. The type of indirect cost which cannot measured and allocated to specific output or work activity is called ......
explain: Overhead costs are indirect costs that cannot be traced or allocated to a specific unit of output or work activity.

q: 11. Material cost is concerned with ......
explain: Materials that go directly into the work are a direct cost.

q: 12. The difference between actual cost of the project with the targeted cost is called ......
explain: Actual cost minus target (budgeted) cost is the cost variance.

q: 13. For the selection of any project the NPV should be ......
explain: A project is acceptable if NPV is zero or more; the minimum acceptable NPV is 0. A negative NPV is rejected, so option b cannot be right.

q: 14. If Interest rate is 1% per month then the effective interest rate is ......
explain: Effective annual rate = (1.01)^12 - 1 = 12.68%, which is more than the nominal 12% because of monthly compounding.

q: 15. If NPV is +ve then, NFV is ......
explain: NFV = NPV x (1+i)^n, and (1+i)^n is always positive, so NFV has the same sign as NPV.

q: 16. The difference of discounted benefit and cost is called ......
explain: NPV = present value of benefits minus present value of costs.

q: 17. Minimum NPV for selection of any project should be ......
explain: The lowest NPV at which a project is still acceptable is zero (NPV >= 0). Note: question number is inferred from order, as it is cropped in the scan.

q: 18. As the present worth of the project increases the project becomes more feasible ......
explain: Higher present worth means greater net economic gain, so the project is more feasible economically.

q: 19. For the selection of any project minimum future worth should be ......
explain: Future worth must be zero or positive for acceptance, so the minimum is 0.

q: 20. Internal rate of return should ......
explain: The project earns IRR while funds cost the borrowing rate, so IRR should be higher than the borrowing rate to create value.

q: 21. Project is assumed as feasible if ......
options: IRR is greater than borrow rate
IRR is lesser than borrow rate
IRR is equal to borrow rate
explain: A project is feasible when its IRR exceeds the cost of borrowing.

q: 22. At what condition project is good ......
options: IRR equal to the discount rate
explain: If IRR is greater than the discount rate, NPV at that discount rate is positive, so the project is good.

q: 23. If P, A and F represents present value, annual payment and future value respectively, then the present worth factor is ......
explain: P/A is the (series) present worth factor, converting a uniform annual payment to present value. Note: Q23 and Q24 are worded alike; the key gives a for Q23 and b for Q24.

q: 24. If P, F and A represents present value and annual payment and future value respectively, then the present worth factor is ......
explain: P/F is the single-payment present worth factor, converting a future sum to present value: P/F = 1/(1+i)^n.

q: 25. If P, F and A represents present value and annual payment and future value respectively, then the Compound amount factor is ......
explain: F/P is the single-payment compound amount factor and F/A is the series compound amount factor, so the key accepts both a and c.

q: 26. If P, F and A represents present value and annual payment and future value respectively, then the Sinking amount factor is ......
explain: The sinking fund factor is A/F, the annual deposit needed to accumulate a given future sum.

q: 27. If P, F and A represents present value and annual payment and future value respectively, then the Capital recovery factor is ......
explain: The capital recovery factor is A/P, the equal annual payment that recovers a present sum.

q: 28. For the selection of any project which criteria is followed ......
explain: IRR, NPV and B/C ratio are all standard criteria for project selection.

q: 29. For the selection of any project which one is mostly used ......
explain: The key marks IRR as the most widely used criterion. Note: many textbooks name NPV; follow the key.

q: 30. For the analysis of any project net present value may be ......
explain: During analysis NPV can come out positive, zero or negative; the sign then decides acceptance.

q: 31. For selection of the project net present value should be ......
explain: A project is selected when its NPV is positive, meaning benefits exceed costs.

q: 32. During analysis of any project, numerical value of net present worth is found negative then, internal rate of return should be ......
explain: A negative NPW at a trial rate means the IRR is lower than that rate, so a lower discount rate must be tried. The key marks a.

q: 33. In a project equal investment is done to obtain a fixed amount it in the future, this amount is known as ......
explain: Equal periodic deposits that accumulate to a fixed future sum form a sinking fund.

q: 34. During the calculation of IRR, NPV should be ......
explain: IRR is by definition the discount rate at which NPV equals zero.

q: 35. In a project selection ERR should be ......
explain: The key marks ERR > 0 (a positive external rate of return) as the condition for selection.

q: 36. Break even analysis is that Limited form of ......
explain: Break-even analysis finds the value of one variable at which the decision changes, which is a limited form of sensitivity analysis.

q: 37. Cost which are independent of output and no alteration by the change in production level are called ......
explain: Fixed costs do not change with the level of output.

q: 38. Net present value is defined as total present value of ...... of cash flows.
explain: NPV is the total present value of the net amount (benefits minus costs) of cash flows.

q: 39. Discounting is the process of ......
options: determine the future value of a cash flow
finding the present value of a cash flow
find the series of equal periodic payment
explain: Discounting converts a future cash flow to its present value.

q: 40. The financial analysis help to judge ......
options: the operational efficiency of the firm
the financial position of the firm
explain: Financial analysis shows both the operating efficiency and the financial position of the firm.

q: 41. In the process of Selecting public project the criteria usually adopted are ......
explain: Public projects are judged on both economic (national benefit) and financial (cash viability) evaluation.

q: 42. The ratio obtained by dividing quick assets by current liabilities is called ......
explain: Quick assets divided by current liabilities is the acid test (quick) ratio.

q: 43. The ratio of current assets to current liabilities is known as ......
explain: Current assets divided by current liabilities is the current ratio.

q: 44. Sensitivity analysis is ......
options: the ratio of benefit to cost using either present worth or annual cash flow calculation
condition under which the alternative are equivalent
examination of the range of values for some parameter determine their effect on particular decision
to change one too many estimate to see what the result is
explain: Sensitivity analysis examines how varying a parameter over a range affects the decision.

q: 45. Mostly used risk analysis technique in engineering is ......
explain: Monte Carlo simulation, which uses probability distributions of inputs, is the key's answer for the most used risk analysis technique.

q: 46. Main objective of sensitivity analysis of a project is to examine the ......
explain: Sensitivity analysis tests how uncertainty in inputs affects the project result.

q: 47. The benefits that is forgone by engaging the same resource in chosen activity instead of engaging the same resource in the forgone activity is known as ......
explain: Opportunity cost is the benefit given up by using a resource in one activity instead of its best alternative.

q: 48. Compounding is the process of converting ......
explain: Compounding moves a present value forward to a future value using F = P(1+i)^n.

q: 49. Discounting is the process of converting ......
explain: Discounting brings a future value back to its present value using P = F/(1+i)^n.

q: 50. The cost that differs to alternatives is called ......
explain: The key as I read it marks d (opportunity cost). Note: 'differential cost' (option c) is the usual textbook term for a cost that differs between alternatives, so please verify this one against a clearer image of the key.

q: 51. The benefit cost ratio is ......
options: superior to all of the above method
explain: A higher discount rate lowers the present worth of future benefits more than costs, so B/C falls as the discount rate rises.

q: 52. For any project to be feasible ......
options: annual worth should be equal to zero
payback period should be equal to or less than 5 year
explain: A project is feasible when its present worth is positive.

q: 53. Net present value is a term widely used in ......
explain: The key marks project cost analysis (c): NPV is a term used in project cost-benefit evaluation.

q: 54. For a government funded development project the most important factor to be considered is ......
explain: Government-funded development projects are justified mainly on wider social and political benefits (key answer b).

q: 55. The discount rate that makes the net present value equal to zero is known as ......
explain: IRR is the discount rate at which NPV = 0.

q: 56. The annuity which refers to debt payment for recovering the initial amount or capital in equal periodical payments, is known as ......
explain: A capital recovery annuity is the equal periodic payment that repays an initial capital with interest.

q: 57. In economic marginal cost is change in total cost that arises when the quantity produced changes by ......
explain: Marginal cost is the change in total cost for a one-unit change in output.

q: 58. If the percentage fall in the quantity demanded is greater than the percentage rise in the price changed ......
options: is not related with the discount rate
explain: Demand is elastic here (fall in quantity bigger than rise in price), so total revenue falls.

q: 59. For a financial institution the most important study of the project to be taken for Risk Management is ......
explain: Key answer a: project appraisal is the study a financial institution relies on to manage lending risk.

q: 60. Excessive spending power of consumers that pulls prices up is called ......
explain: When too much demand chases limited goods, prices are pulled up: demand-pull inflation.

q: 61. The ratio analysis of construction firm is used for the analysis by ......
explain: Key answer a: ratio analysis is a tool of financial analysis.

q: 62. In economic the change in total cost that arises when the quantity produced changes by 1 unit is called ......
explain: This is the definition of marginal cost.

q: 63. If P is the principal amount, i is the ratio of interest and n is the number of periods in a year then the interest factor is ......
explain: For simple interest, amount = P(1 + ni), so the interest factor is 1 + ni.

q: 64. If a seller recovers his capital along with accumulated compensating interest not in one single lump sum payment but in a periodical equal payments, overtime ......
options: capital recovery annuity is a valid
present work annuity is a valid
sinking fund annuity is a valid
explain: Recovering capital plus interest through equal periodic payments is a capital recovery annuity.

q: 65. The sinking fund factor is ......
explain: Sinking fund factor A/F = i / ((1+i)^n - 1).

q: 66. The capital recovery factor of capital recovery annuity is ......
explain: Capital recovery factor A/P = i(1+i)^n / ((1+i)^n - 1). Note: the minus sign in option a is smudged in the scan; I read it as the standard formula.

q: 67. In a cash flow diagram ......
options: time 0 is considered to be present
time 1 is considered to be end of the past period 1
a vertical arrow pointing up indicates a positive each cash flow
explain: Time 0 is the present, time 1 marks the end of period 1, and an upward arrow is a positive cash flow, so all statements hold.

q: 68. Present worth annuity (PWA) is generally is generally known as ......
explain: The key accepts all of the listed names for a present worth annuity.

q: 69. Pick up the element of cost from the following ......
explain: Direct material, direct labour and overhead are all elements of cost.

q: 70. The inverse of sinking fund factor is ......
explain: Sinking fund factor is A/F; its inverse F/A is the series compound amount factor.

q: 71. The wages of supervisor and material handlers are charged as ......
explain: Supervisor and material handler wages cannot be charged to a specific product, so they are charged as overhead.

q: 72. The sunk cost include ......
options: an invested capital that cannot be retrieved
explain: Sunk costs are past expenditures and unrecoverable capital; they should not affect future decisions.

q: 73. In a cash flow series ......
options: uniform gradient signifies that and income or disbursement changed by the same amount in each interest period
either an increase or decrease in the amount of cash flow is called the gradient
the gradient in a cash flow may be positive or negative
explain: A gradient is a constant increase or decrease in cash flow per period, so all statements are correct.
